First run of .\test.ps1 app showed a transient failure in ThumbnailItemViewModelTests.Dispose_WithLoadedBitmap_DoesNotThrow (unrelated to WP-005 changes). The test passed on the second full run and in isolation. This is a known Avalonia headless flakiness pattern; not caused by WP-005 changes.

summary: Reviewed both test files. FakeFfmpegRunner design is elegant — returning Task.CompletedTask without creating the output file correctly exercises the file-existence guard in InitializeAsync without disk I/O. CanNudge tests cover all three conditions of the property. InitializeAsync tests directly assert CallCount and LastPositionMs against the fake runner. The new null-path test in BookmarksPanelViewModelTests rounds out the coverage. One medium-priority improvement flagged: FakeFfmpegRunner is duplicated with PlayerViewModelTests.cs — a shared TestHelper would eliminate the redundancy. No blocking issues.

comments.note: FakeFfmpegRunner design is excellent: returning Task.CompletedTask without creating the output file correctly exercises the if (File.Exists(tempPath)) guard in InitializeAsync. The bitmap-load step is skipped when the file is absent, so the test verifies the full guard path without disk I/O. The comment on the class explaining this behaviour is helpful.

The four CanNudge tests collectively provide complete combinatorial coverage of the CanNudge property's three conditions: no-runner, runner+null-path, edit-mode+path, create-mode+runner+path. Together with the pre-existing CanNudge_WithoutFfmpegRunner_IsFalse test, all branches are covered.

FakeFfmpegRunner is duplicated as a private inner class between BookmarkSettingsViewModelTests.cs and PlayerViewModelTests.cs. The Developer noted this as an improvement candidate. Promoting a shared FakesFfmpegRunner to tests/VideoIndexer.App.Tests/TestHelpers/ would eliminate the duplication. Not blocking, but worth a follow-up.
